chapter_theme: Verses 61-80 set out reverence to Veda-knowers, elders and the vulnerable, and then a long code of conduct in the presence of the great: in the great house, before the lord and in his counsel, the attendant governs gaze, gesture, speech and the body itself.
structure_note: 61-64 reverence to Veda-knowers, elders and those owed the road; 65 the senses and kinswomen; 66-79 conduct in attendance on the great and the lord; 80 forms of address.

61.reading: The verse reports it as the settled view of those versed in the treatises that the knowers of the four Vedas, who came by the order of heaven, are to be treated in the higher way, as one's own elders are.
61.nuance: The verse does not name the brahmin by a birth word; it names him by the four Vedas and by a coming வான்முறையான், 'by the order of heaven', so the rank is grounded in a sacred origin rather than in conduct. குரவர் here takes the sense verse 16 gives it, the five elders worshipped as gods.

norm.note: a rule of the period that ranks the Veda-knowers with one's own elders by a heaven-given order

62.reading: The verse reports that the elders call three acts the ஆசாரம் owed to elders, stated in essence: bowing at the feet, attendance at the proper time, and rising when they come.
62.nuance: சமயம் is the doubtful item: it can be waiting on the elder at the fit time, or keeping the elder's own creed; the first fits the bodily acts beside it. The verse says the three were told சாரத்தால், as the gist, so it offers them as a summary of reverence, not a full code.

items.claim: bowing at the feet is ஆசாரம் owed to elders
attendance at the proper time is ஆசாரம் owed to elders
rising up at their coming is ஆசாரம் owed to elders

63.reading: The verse names three things as the path seen by those who saw the right manner: caring for those who have renounced, modesty, and not speaking before elders, even by lapse, of what one has learned.
63.nuance: The third item is a restraint on learning itself: the learned man keeps his learning silent in the presence of elders, so learning is ranked below reverence.

items.claim: caring for those who have renounced belongs to the right path
modesty belongs to the right path
not voicing one's own learning before elders, even by lapse, belongs to the right path

64.reading: The verse names eight to whom one gives way on the road (brahmins, ascetics, those carrying loads, the sick, the old, the young, cows and women) and says those who step fully aside for them are called praiseworthy among births.
64.nuance: பார்ப்பார் is a birth term and heads the list, followed by the ascetic; the rest are the burdened and the weak, so a rank by birth and a care for the vulnerable are given one gesture. பிறப்பிடைப் போற்றி may mean praised among men, or praised in their births to come; the verse does not settle it.

items.claim: brahmins are to be given way to
ascetics are to be given way to
those carrying loads are to be given way to
the sick are to be given way to
the old are to be given way to
the young are to be given way to
cows are to be given way to
women are to be given way to

norm.note: a road rule of the period that puts brahmins first among those one gives way to

65.reading: The verse reports that the worthy should not stay alone even with their own mother, daughter or sister, because the five senses are hard to hold back.
65.nuance: The reason given is not the woman's conduct but the man's senses: even சான்றார் are not trusted to restrain the five, so the rule removes the occasion rather than relying on restraint.

norm.note: a rule of the period separating men from their nearest kinswomen when alone

66.reading: The verse says that those who mean to live on to the end (in a great one's service) are not angered when stopped at the gate, do not take excessive liberties of intimacy, are not careless at the giving of gifts, do not dress as their lord does, and do not cut in between to go and join another.
66.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
66.nuance: கடை is the gate of the great house, which sets the verse in attendance on a lord. கோலநேர் செய்யார் is read as not matching the lord's dress; இடையறுத்துப் போகிப் பிறனொருவன் சேரார் can be not breaking off to attach oneself to another patron, or not passing between two people to reach a third. கடைபோக வாழ்தும் is survival as much as virtue.

67.reading: The verse says one should not speak a pronouncement about oneself, a retort answering what one's betters have said, or a pronouncement about others, and that speaking them turns into a fault that scars.
67.nuance: The three speeches cover self, superior and third party, so the verse closes off every subject on which one might pronounce; வடுக்குற்றம் makes the fault a lasting mark, not a passing lapse.

68.reading: The verse says they do not take pleasure in what the great take pleasure in, do not enter a house bringing lowly men, and do not speak slightingly even of an undiscerning child in a place where they are not on familiar terms.
68.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
68.nuance: The child that may not be slighted is most naturally the great house's own child; தம்மோடு அளவளாவில்லா இடத்து limits the rules to a house where one is not intimate, so the verse is about the stranger's caution in another's household.

69.reading: The verse says they do not show anger or sulk, do not stand facing the great one, do not speak of their own affairs to him in private, and do not say 'we know what is pleasant', even if he says without kindness that the crow is white.
69.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
69.nuance: The closing clause gives the measure of the whole rule: the attendant does not contradict the great one even on a plain falsehood. The verse does not call this truth; it calls it conduct.

70.reading: The verse names five things they do not do in the house of the great: spitting, climbing to a high seat, chewing areca, speaking out of order, and lying down.
70.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
70.nuance: வளர்ச்சி is read as lying down (வளர், to sleep); a reading 'growing familiar' is possible. The list mixes bodily acts and speech as one class of liberties.

items.claim: spitting is not done in the house of the great
climbing to a raised place is not done there
chewing areca is not done there
speech out of its proper order is not done there
lying down is not done there

71.reading: The verse says that those of good family do not speak before their lord of their own wealth, learning, lustre and virtue, spreading them out again and again as an enemy would.
71.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
71.nuance: பகைவர்போல் gives the reason: display of one's own excellences before the lord reads as a rival's challenge, so the restraint is prudence. குலமுடையார் makes it a mark of good birth.

72.reading: The verse says that in the house of the great and in a temple they do not bow even to their own elders when they see them, nor when the great go with the deity.
72.nuance: Reverence is ruled by place: where a greater object of worship is present, bowing to another, even to the elders verse 16 says to worship as gods, is withheld. The third line, அணங்கொடு நேர்பெரியார் செல்லுமிடத்து, is hard; it may mean when the great go in procession with the deity.

norm.note: a rule of the period on where obeisance to elders is withheld

73.reading: The verse names laughter, yawning, hawking and sneezing as things they do not do before the great, and says that if done, blame stays fixed.
73.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
73.nuance: Involuntary acts of the body are treated as conduct: the verse holds a man to blame for a sneeze as for a laugh.

items.claim: laughter is not done before the great
yawning is not done before the great
hawking is not done before the great
sneezing is not done before the great

74.reading: The verse says that when the great one stands one stands in restraint, when he sits one does not leave unless sent, one listens with attention when he speaks, and one does not ask again once his word is over.
74.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
74.nuance: The rule on questions is the sharpest: the hearer may not reopen what the great one has closed, so listening is complete when he stops.

75.reading: The verse says that in the house of the great they do not let their garment slip, do not speak with the hand raised, do not look at the women, and do not take in whispered words.
75.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
75.nuance: செவிசொறுண்டார் on line 1 is not a clear word; it may be a scribal form of 'scratching the ear'. The bar on looking at the women of the house sets them inside the lord's domain.

norm.note: a rule of the period barring the attendant's gaze on the women of a great house

76.reading: The verse says that one does not speak hastily, on and on, in false and sprawling ways, or at length, but speaks knowing the right moment, with few syllables that hold the whole sense together.
76.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
76.nuance: செவ்வி is the hearer's fit moment, so brevity and timing are one rule. காலந்தால் on line 3 is unclear, perhaps காலத்தால்.

77.reading: The verse says they do not look at their own body, do not tousle their hair, do not snap their fingers, and look at no body but that of the chief.
77.domain_note: one who attends on the chief (தலைமகன்)
77.nuance: The gaze itself is disciplined: the attendant's eyes belong to the chief, as in verse 75 they may not fall on his women.

78.reading: The verse says they do not take counsel with others in the lord's presence, do not go near the lord or listen in, and if near, stand turned away as if attending to something else.
78.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
78.nuance: Line 3 gives a posture, not only an abstention: one acts out inattention so as to be seen not to be listening.

79.reading: The verse names three things found in the capable: sharing the sorrow when there is sorrow, conducting oneself in joyful ways when there is joy, and, out of loyalty, not entering the house of those who have fallen under wrath.
79.domain_note: one who attends on the great one, the lord or king
79.nuance: The sorrow and joy are most likely the lord's, whose moods the attendant mirrors; செறப்பட்டார் are those who have incurred anger, presumably the lord's, so avoiding their house is loyalty, not unkindness.

items.claim: sorrowing in a time of sorrow is found in the capable
behaving joyfully in a time of joy is found in the capable
not entering the house of those under wrath is found in the capable

80.reading: The verse says that even when provoked they do not utter their elders' names, do not stay long in a house clearing the throat, do not address the great by terms of kinship, and that those who know well do not address even the புலையர் by terms of kinship.
80.nuance: புலையர் is a caste term for a birth-group held outcaste; here it plainly names persons. The final rule withholds kin-address from them as from the great, at the opposite end of rank; முறை may also mean addressing them with honour. நன்கறிவார் repeats the close of verse 6.

norm.note: a rule of the period withholding kinship address from those ranked outcaste

links.note: Kural 134 says a brahmin's birth is ruined when his conduct fails, though a forgotten Veda can be relearned; Acharakkovai 61 says the four-Veda knowers, come by heaven's order, are honoured as one's own elders.
links.teaches: The Kural makes the brahmin's standing hang on conduct and treats the Veda as recoverable, while the Acharakkovai grounds his honour in the Veda and a heavenly origin and names no condition of conduct, so the two disagree on what earns the rank.
links.list_adds: It places the Veda-knowers inside the circle of one's own elders, so reverence for a birth-group is folded into filial reverence, which the couplet never does.

links.note: Verse 16 names the five peerless elders and says to worship them as gods; verse 62 names the three acts of ஆசாரம் owed to elders.
links.teaches: Verse 16 gives the rank and verse 62 the bodily acts by which god-like worship of elders is performed, so the book's worship of elders turns out to be bowing, timely attendance and rising.

links.note: Verse 16 says the elders are to be worshipped as gods; verse 72 says that in a great house or a temple one does not bow even to them.
links.teaches: The god-like worship verse 16 owes to elders gives way where a greater object of worship is present, so the book ranks reverence by place and the elder's claim is not absolute.

links.note: Verse 61 honours the four-Veda knowers as one's own elders; verse 64 puts பார்ப்பார் first among eight to whom one yields the road.
links.teaches: Verse 64 turns 61's honour into a gesture on the road and sets the brahmin at the head of a line of the burdened, the sick and cows, so rank by birth is enacted with the same act as care for the weak.

links.note: Kural 126 says that drawing in the five senses like a tortoise protects for seven births; Acharakkovai 65 says the five are hard to hold even for the worthy, so they must not stay alone with their nearest kinswomen.
links.teaches: Where the Kural trusts restraint of the senses as a power one can gain, the Acharakkovai doubts it even in the worthy and replaces it with a rule that removes the occasion, so self-mastery is backed by avoidance.
links.list_adds: It names mother, daughter and sister as the case, so the doubt about restraint is pressed to the women least suspected, a limit the couplet never tests.

links.note: Kural 700 says intimacy that does the improper because 'we are old friends' brings ruin; Acharakkovai 66 names கழிகிழமை, overstepping intimacy, among the things those who would last in service avoid.
links.teaches: The Kural states the danger of presuming on an old bond; the Acharakkovai puts that danger among gate, gift and dress, showing that presuming on intimacy is one of several small encroachments on a lord's dignity.
links.list_adds: It sets excessive intimacy beside anger at the gate, carelessness at gifts and dressing like the lord, so the couplet's single fault becomes one of a family of encroachments.

links.note: Kural 692 says not desiring what kings desire brings lasting gain through them; Acharakkovai 68 opens with not taking pleasure in what the great take pleasure in.
links.teaches: The couplet gives the rule and its reward; the Acharakkovai shows what it looks like in the house, joined to not bringing low men in and not slighting the house's child, so not rivalling the lord's pleasures is part of guarding his household.
links.list_adds: It joins the rule to two others about the great man's house, so restraint of desire is placed among household courtesies rather than left as a maxim.

links.note: Kural 698 says not to slight one as younger or as kin but to act by the light he stands in; Acharakkovai 68 says not to speak slightingly even of an undiscerning child.
links.teaches: Read together, the young one the Kural warns against slighting can be a mere child of the great house, so the rule against belittling youth reaches down to the child who cannot yet understand.
links.list_adds: It makes the child's undiscerning state the extreme case, not only youth, and ties the rule to the place where one is not intimate.

links.note: Pazhamozhi 281 says that even when an angry king does what one does not want, one should not act on one's resentment, for no one wakes a sleeping tiger; Acharakkovai 69 says one does not sulk or contradict even if the great one says the crow is white.
links.teaches: Pazhamozhi bars acting on resentment when the king wrongs one; the Acharakkovai extends the bar to speech and face when he speaks falsely, so the attendant's silence covers both injury and untruth.

links.note: Naladiyar 164 says those who anger the great do not escape even in a fortress, as the snake in its crevice dreads thunder; Acharakkovai 69 lists the small signs of displeasure one must not show before the great.
links.teaches: The Naladiyar gives the reason the Acharakkovai's courtesies are owed: the great one's anger reaches anywhere, so the rule not to sulk or contradict is a defence, not only a manner.
links.list_adds: It breaks the single danger into a list of guarded acts, sulking, facing, private talk and contradiction, so the quatrain's dread becomes a code of gestures.

links.note: Naladiyar 170 says the fitting quality of one who has some excellence is restraint; Acharakkovai 71 says those of good family do not spread out their wealth, learning, lustre and virtue before the lord.
links.teaches: The Naladiyar makes restraint the proper dress of excellence in general; the Acharakkovai names the place where it is tested, before the lord, and the risk of failing it, being taken for an enemy.
links.list_adds: It names four excellences, wealth, learning, lustre and virtue, as alike to be kept silent before the lord, and gives a reason, looking like an enemy, that the quatrain lacks.

links.note: Verse 63 bars speaking one's learning before elders; verse 71 bars displaying learning and three other excellences before the lord.
links.teaches: The same silence about one's learning is owed in the house to elders and at court to the lord, so the book treats display of learning as a breach of rank in both spheres.

links.note: Kural 694 says to suppress whispers and shared smiles before the great; Acharakkovai 73 bars laughter, yawning, hawking and sneezing before them.
links.teaches: The Kural bars the laugh as a sign that may be misread; the Acharakkovai puts it with yawning and sneezing, which carry no meaning, so the presence of the great governs the body itself and not only what it signals.
links.list_adds: It joins a meaningful act, laughter, to involuntary ones, so the couplet's guard against misread signs becomes a guard on the body as such.

links.note: Kural 694 says to suppress whispers before the great; Acharakkovai 75 says that in the house of the great one does not take in whispered words, nor look at the women, nor let the garment slip.
links.teaches: The Kural forbids whispering in the presence of the great; the Acharakkovai also forbids receiving a whisper, so the listener is as guilty as the speaker.
links.list_adds: It sets the whisper beside the gaze on the women and the slipping garment, so the couplet's rule on speech becomes one of several guards on eye, ear and body in the great house.

links.note: Kural 696 says to speak knowing the mood and the time, what is needed and not disliked; Acharakkovai 76 says to speak at the right moment with few syllables that hold the whole sense.
links.teaches: The Kural asks for the right time and the right matter; the Acharakkovai adds the right length, so speech before the great is judged by moment, content and brevity together.
links.list_adds: It lists four faults of manner, haste, going on, falsehood and sprawl, before giving the positive rule, so the couplet's advice is defined against its failures.

links.note: Kural 695 says not to listen in or press for anything, but to hear a secret when it is released; Acharakkovai 78 says not to take counsel with others or listen in, and if near, to stand turned away as if busy with something else.
links.teaches: The Kural states the inner restraint; the Acharakkovai gives the posture that makes it visible, standing turned away, so not listening must also be seen not to listen.
links.list_adds: It adds a staged posture of attention elsewhere to the bar on listening, which the couplet does not have.

links.note: Verse 6 lists புலை among five sights barred in எச்சில்; verse 80 bars addressing புலையர் by kinship terms, and both close on நன்கறிவார்.
links.teaches: Verse 80's plural personal form with a verb of address shows the book uses this root for persons, which weighs toward reading புலை in verse 6 as the outcaste person rather than an impure thing.

source_issues: Verse 64 is lacking on the source site the corpus was checked against (tool flag site_diff); it is marked from the core text.
Verse 66 line 4 (கடைபோக வாழ்துமென் பார்) recurs as verse 83 line 4: a formulaic close, flagged as a repeated line.
Verse 75 line 1 செவிசொறுண்டார் is not a clear word, perhaps a scribal form of ear-scratching.
Verse 76 line 3 காலந்தால் is unclear, perhaps காலத்தால்.
Verse 72 line 3 அணங்கொடு நேர்பெரியார் செல்லுமிடத்து is hard to construe.
